With the corrosion allowance duly added, the wall thickness of the absorber comes to some 44 mm, and it is the pressure case rather than the temperature case that effectively sets the metal required. The gasket choice, it turns out, is considerably narrower than the flange schedule might suggest. Of the two materials that have been carried forward, one is rated to a higher temperature limit than the other, and the comparison between them is made on the basis of that limit alone.

On that basis, the higher-rated material emerges as the preferred option for the absorber flanges. The design temperature is set by the regeneration case, and at that temperature the lower-rated material leaves precious little margin between its limit and the duty in question. Attention then turns to the lean solvent pump, where the margin on the suction side narrows as the $\Delta P$ through the suction line grows, and where the available NPSH has yet to be set against the requirement of the pump itself, a matter that is closely bound up with the suction line sizing that has still to be finalised

With the corrosion allowance added, the wall thickness of the absorber is 44 mm, and the pressure case rather than the temperature case sets the metal required. The gasket choice is narrower than the flange schedule suggests. Of the two materials carried forward, one is rated to a higher temperature limit than the other, and the comparison is made on that limit alone. Sealing stress, mechanical properties, and cost are not in question between the two, and the flange faces and bolting are common to both, so the temperature limit is the whole of the decision that remains open at this stage of the design.

On that basis the higher-rated material is preferred for the absorber flanges. The design temperature is set by the regeneration case, and at that temperature the lower-rated material leaves little margin between its limit and the duty. Attention then turns to the lean solvent pump, where the margin at the suction side narrows as the $\Delta P$ through the suction line grows, and where the available NPSH has still to be set against the pump's requirement, with the suction line size feeding back into the $\Delta P$ allowed for the circuit as a whole
